newsitem.title: FRANCE: INTERVIEW-Alcatel plans Euro defence talks.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Alcatel plans Euro defence talks.

text.p: French engineering group Alcatel-Alsthom plans to hold urgent talks with European defence companies if its joint bid with Dassault in the privatisation of Thomson-CSF is accepted.

Chairman Serge Tchuruk told Reuters in an interview that while he had rejected an offer by Daimler-Benz Aerospace (DASA) to strike a deal prior to the government's sale of a 58-percent stake in Thomson-CSF, he was open to talks later.
DASA has concluded an exclusive deal with rival Lagardere, the other group that bid for Thomson-CSF on May 7.

"With DASA, they wanted to conclude a deal prior to the acceptance of our offer (by the government) and we did not want that," Tchuruk said after a joint news conference with Dassault Industries chairman Serge Dassault.
"If the Alcatel bid is accepted, we will start discussions with DASA afterwards. And they will take place with an open mind," he said.
"After all, we are industrialists and we are here to do business. DASA is an important partner," he said.

"In the future, with the large Thomson-CSF it will be necessary to deal with DASA and with GEC. That will have to take place in the coming months, we do not have the time to wait for years," Tchuruk said.
"We have to resume our talks with DASA and GEC with an open mind. We will have to take account of national defence interests and come with even-handed solutions," he said.

At the news conference, Tchuruk and Dassault said their offer was better than Lagardere's because it would leave Thomson-CSF intact, better preserve French defence interests and because Alcatel and Dassault could more easily finance the deal.

"It is very clear. We have the financial means for this operation without any problems, that is not the case for Lagardere. Lagardere needs to make compromises, which are unbalanced, in order to finance the operation," Tchuruk said.
"I'm not totally closed to making compromises but for compromises made because of other considerations than financial worries," he said.
Tchuruk said Alcatel shareholders had nothing to fear from its bid for Thomson-CSF.
"I have told my shareholders that the Thomson operations would not at all lead to a situation of excessive debt nor reduce the earnings per share," he said.
"I have made that commitment to my shareholders and I will keep that commitment," he said.
Alcatel Alsthom earlier on Tuesday reported a 12.1 percent increase in first quarter sales, or a 5.6 percent rise on a like-for-like basis.
Tchuruk said the sales increase "shows we are on the road to recovery. There is still a long way to go but we are on the right track."
He added that the 10 percent increase in telecoms orders in the first quarter was important for the company.
He said he was taken aback by market reaction to the sales figures, with Alcatel up 5.12 percent at 678 francs at 1136 GMT.
"I'm surprised that the market is surprised when we announce that we are doing things like we said we would," he said.
Asked about the market reaction to the swings and round-abouts in the Thomson-CSF privatisation saga, Tchuruk said the reaction had become less overtly negative.
"At the start the share went down when people thought we would win and rose when the other camp was in favour. At the moment it is not so clear-cut anymore," he said.
